ai.title: Version bump 1.0.495
ai.summary: Package version in `npm-app/release/package.json` updated to 1.0.495. No functional code changes included in this commit.

eli5.text: A new release of the AI coding assistant shipped that fixes the tool so it no longer crashes or returns empty results when a task can't be completed, and it also streamlines how the assistant connects to other code tools. If you use the assistant, you might notice it handles errors more quietly instead of failing outright. These changes went live with the latest version that most users will receive automatically.

ai.title: sdk.run() returns RunState instead of null on errors
ai.summary: sdk.run() and CodebuffClient.run() now return Promise<RunState> instead of Promise<RunState | null>. Error paths in run.ts resolve with a structured RunState containing sessionState and an error output object, replacing null returns. Scope covers sdk/src/client.ts and sdk/src/run.ts. handlePromptResponse propagates initialSessionState to error resolutions.

eli5.text: When the assistant you use through a custom app or integration hits a problem and can't finish its task, it now returns a clear 'here's what happened and where we left off' result instead of just stopping silently with nothing to show for it. This means apps built on the SDK will no longer receive an empty result that they have to special-case, and can always expect a proper structured response, even when something goes wrong.

ai.title: @codebuff/sdk 0.3.1 removes null return from run
ai.summary: @codebuff/sdk 0.3.1 changes `CodebuffClient.run` to return an object with `output.type === 'error'` instead of `null` on failure. README examples updated to check `run1.output.type` and use `zod/v4` imports. Breaking change for error handling logic in existing integrations.

eli5.text: When the coding assistant fails to complete a task, it now returns a clear error report with details instead of silently giving you nothing back. This affects anyone building tools that plug into the assistant through the developer kit, who previously had to check whether the result was empty and now must read the error type and message from the returned object. If you looked at the updated examples, you'd see the failure-handling logic switched to inspecting the result object and printing the error message it carries.

ai.title: open package replaces spawn in npm-app client
ai.summary: Added `open` package to `npm-app/package.json` and replaced platform-specific `spawn` calls with `await open(loginUrl)` in `npm-app/src/client.ts`. Switches to a cross-platform URL opener for reliable browser launching across Windows, macOS, and Linux during login. Scope limited to `npm-app` client logic.

eli5.text: When someone tries to sign in, the app now opens their web browser to the login page using a single built-in method that works the same way on Windows, Mac, and Linux computers, instead of picking a different command for each operating system. This affects only the login step of the npm-app client, which is the part that talks to the service behind the scenes. The new approach replaced a handful of lines that tried to guess the right system command, so you would notice nothing in the app's look or menus, but the login window is more likely to open on the first try no matter what computer you use.

ai.title: SDK 0.3.2 simplify README examples
ai.summary: Bump @codebuff/sdk to 0.3.2. Simplify sdk/README.md by removing verbose console logs, clarifying handleEvent comments, and restructuring error/output handling in examples. Scope: sdk/README.md, sdk/package.json. Detail: cwd marked optional in second example.

eli5.text: If you've been reading the example guide to the programming toolkit, the walkthrough now skips the extra print statements that were showing each step in detail, so the example code stays focused on the main actions instead of cluttering the screen with every behind-the-scenes event. The example also no longer requires you to specify the folder your program runs from, making the starting steps simpler. A small version number for the toolkit itself went up to mark these documentation and setup tweaks.

ai.title: Streaming logger for programmatic agent steps
ai.summary: Added `logger` interface to `AgentStepContext` and `handleSteps` generator, enabling real-time debug/info/warn/error logs from agent code. Backend `runProgrammatic-step.ts` injects streaming logger that sends `handlesteps-log-chunk` actions to frontend via WebSocket. QuickJS sandbox exposes `_loggerHandler` for string-based generators to call native logging. Affects `.agents/types`, `backend/src/run-programmatic-step.ts`, `backend/src/util/quickjs-sandbox.ts`, `common/src/actions.ts`.

eli5.text: When an AI assistant built with Codebuff works through a multi-step coding task, it can now stream live status messages, like 'reading file...', 'planning edits...', or 'found an error', directly to anyone watching the process in a web browser or app. Previously, these behind-the-scenes logs stayed hidden in the backend until the whole task finished; now they appear in real time over the connection as the work unfolds. This affects developers building custom coding assistants with Codebuff's agent tools, especially those using simple text-based scripts (QuickJS) or full TypeScript setups. The feature works today: log messages written by the agent's code are now sent instantly to the frontend instead of being held back.

ai.title: Version 1.0.496 ships SDK error handling, streaming logger
ai.summary: Release 1.0.496 bundles several user-visible improvements over 1.0.495. The @codebuff/sdk package (now at 0.3.2) no longer returns null on errors from run() and CodebuffClient.run(); instead those paths resolve with a structured RunState object containing sessionState and an error output object whose type equals 'error'. This is a breaking change for integrations that checked for null on failure, and the SDK README was simplified to demonstrate checking run1.output.type and using zod/v4 imports. The npm-app client now uses the cross-platform open package to launch login URLs via await open(loginUrl) instead of platform-specific spawn calls, and a streaming logger interface was added to AgentStepContext and handleSteps, enabling real-time debug/info/warn/error logs from agent code through handlesteps-log-chunk WebSocket actions.
ai.evidence: The diff shows only a version field change in `npm-app/release/package.json` from 1.0.495 to 1.0.496, with no functional code changes in this commit. The release updates section lists user-visible changes shipped since 1.0.495: SDK error returns becoming structured RunState objects, breaking error-handling changes in @codebuff/sdk 0.3.1, the open package replacing spawn in npm-app login, simplified SDK README examples, and a streaming logger interface for programmatic agent steps.

eli5.text: This release makes the developer tools more reliable and gives you better visibility into what happens when things go wrong. The main improvements are: error reporting that now gives you a clear, structured summary of failures instead of a blank result, a smoother login experience that opens your browser automatically across Windows, Mac, and Linux, simplified setup instructions that are easier to follow, and real-time logging so you can watch the AI's step-by-step progress as it works. Upgrading means fewer confusing blank screens when errors occur, a login flow that just works no matter what computer you use, and the ability to see live updates of what the AI is doing instead of waiting silently for a final answer.
